10 · Stress test of the team financial model: which levers put 2033 at risk¶

The team financial model (rev. 13, documented in notes/financial-model.md, PR #20) reaches 100 % in 2033 with programme capex of EUR 1,943.5 m. As built it draws a straight line to the target year and assumes every bus it needs is delivered and paid for. Here it is ported unchanged (the reproduction check below) and every run in this section uses rev. 13 as documented (D9, 24 Nov 2026): the pitch and the report quote it. File 4's conventions are run beside it as a comparison only (10.3): fleet 2,210 (D1), e-bus renewals at a 13-year life (D2), constant 2025 prices and no EU grants. File 4 cannot take rev. 13's values, because the brief fixes File 4's capex in constant 2025 euros (so no 2 %/yr price growth) and takes the fleet from the register (2,210, not 2,239); rev. 13 is the financial plan built on top of it. Each year's additions are capped by three real limits:

  1. Deliveries: buses EMT can take delivery of in a year, renewals included.
  2. Chargers: a bus is only added if a charging position is in place (the model only flags the gap).
  3. Money: self-financing plus EU grants plus a borrowing cap, after depot works are paid.

Each lever is then moved between an optimistic and a pessimistic value (ranges and sources in LEVER_EVIDENCE). Supplementary: printed only, never written to File 1–4.

In [26]:
# Team financial model, rev. 13 (PR #20, notes/financial-model.md): inputs as documented there, labels mapped
# Official -> V, Calculated -> D, Assumption -> A, Brief -> V. Only the levers below are new.
FM = assume("Financial model rev. 13 inputs", dict(
    target_year=2033, fleet_total=2239, h2_buses=10, ebuses_2025=456, ebuses_added_2026=70, ebuses_added_2027=65,
    price_12m=615, price_18m=800, artic_share=0.08, escalation=0.02, renew_2031_35=329,
    retrofit_keur=110, high_keur=203, new_depot_keur=353, eu_grant_share=0.20, self_fin=35,
    eib_share=0.50, eib_rate=0.03, gb_coupon=0.036), "D",
    "notes/financial-model.md (PR #20), sheet Assumptions; types per row there (fleet 2,239 is EMT's accounts mix, not the "
    "2,210 register baseline of File 4)", "section 10 only")
FM_REV13 = dict(FM)                    # as documented, for the reproduction check only
_bev = fleet25.loc[fleet25.fuelType == "EL", "age_years"]
RENEW_LIFE = int(((_bev > NB01["bus_life"] - 10) & (_bev <= NB01["bus_life"] - 5)).sum())
FM_ALIGNED = assume("Financial model on File 4's conventions (comparison only, D9)", {**FM, **dict(
    fleet_total=NB01["fleet"], ebuses_2025=B25["n_bev"], escalation=0.0, eu_grant_share=0.0, renew_2031_35=RENEW_LIFE)}, "D",
    f"D1 fleet {NB01['fleet']:,}; D2 {NB01['bus_life']}-year life, so e-buses renewed in 2031-35 = register e-buses aged "
    f"{NB01['bus_life'] - 10}-{NB01['bus_life'] - 5} at end 2025 ({RENEW_LIFE}; rev. 13 used EMT's 329 at 12 years); D4 EUR 110k per "
    "position (unchanged); constant 2025 prices (no 2 %/yr growth); EU grants 0 in the base (none awarded for 2027+)",
    "section 10.3 comparison only; FM stays rev. 13", "rev. 13 is the base of every other run in section 10")
FM_CNG = [(None, 2027, 300), (576, 2029, 300), (460, 2032, 300), (520, 2034, 291)]   # cohorts: buses, natural retirement, EUR k;
# the oldest cohort is the remainder of the baseline's CNG fleet (217 at 2,239; 192 at 2,210)
FM_YEARS = range(2026, 2041)          # to 2040, so a slip past 2035 shows as a year

# Risk levers. Defaults reproduce the model as built (no limits, no delays).
UNLIMITED = 10_000
LEVER_EVIDENCE = assume("Lever ranges (optimistic / likely / pessimistic)", {
    "delivery_cap (buses/yr)": (300, 230, 159), "borrow_cap (EUR m/yr)": (250, 150, 100),
    "Las Tablas delay (yr)": (0, 1, 2), "Entrevias delay (yr)": (0, 1, 2), "other retrofits delay (yr)": (0, 1, 2),
    "La Elipa delay (yr)": (0, 0, 1), "price vs tender max": (0.9, 1.0, "1.0 and +4 %/yr")}, "A",
    "Deliveries: EMT fleet register 382 in 2018, about 257 a year in 2019-20; 159 kept as a low case (financial-model.md s.8, notebook 04 s.1); "
    "borrowing: pitch condition 4 (about EUR 150 m/yr); delays: London grid connections 9+ months per garage, no Madrid "
    "requests filed yet, Las Tablas design contract 12 months (financial-model.md s.8); prices are tender maximums",
    "section 10 tornado and realistic case")

def fm_cng(A):
    """CNG cohorts for the baseline in A: the oldest cohort takes the remainder."""
    rest = A["fleet_total"] - A["h2_buses"] - A["ebuses_2025"] - sum(n for n, _, _ in FM_CNG[1:])
    return [(rest, FM_CNG[0][1], FM_CNG[0][2])] + FM_CNG[1:]

def fm_run(**over):
    """Financial model rev. 13 with each year's additions capped by deliveries, chargers in place and money left after depot
    works (self-financing + EU grants + borrowing cap). Returns (summary dict, year table)."""
    A = {**FM, "delivery_cap": UNLIMITED, "borrow_cap": UNLIMITED, "delay_entrevias": 0, "delay_las_tablas": 0,
         "delay_la_elipa": 0, "delay_retrofit": 0, "price_factor": 1.0, "charger_keur": None,
         "lease_share": 0.0, "caas_share": 0.0, "lease_rate": 0.05, "lease_term": 12, **over}
    annuity = A["lease_rate"] / (1 - (1 + A["lease_rate"]) ** -A["lease_term"]) if A["lease_rate"] else 1 / A["lease_term"]
    ze_max, rk = A["fleet_total"] - A["h2_buses"], A["charger_keur"] or A["retrofit_keur"]
    proj = {"Sanchinarro": (114, 12.58, 2026, 2027), "Carabanchel 27": (27, 27 * 83 / 1000, 2026, 2026),
            "La Elipa": (318, 112.12, 2026, 2029 + A["delay_la_elipa"]),
            "Entrevias": (465, 465 * rk / 1000, 2027, 2028 + A["delay_entrevias"]),
            "Las Tablas": (650, 650 * A["new_depot_keur"] / 1000, 2028, 2031 + A["delay_las_tablas"])}
    rest = ze_max - A["ebuses_2025"] - sum(v[0] for v in proj.values())
    proj["Remaining retrofit"] = (rest, rest * rk / 1000, 2028, 2030 + A["delay_retrofit"])
    cont = ((465 + rest) * (A["high_keur"] - A["retrofit_keur"]) / 1000, 2027, 2030 + max(A["delay_entrevias"], A["delay_retrofit"]))
    phased = lambda t, s, e, y: t / (e - s + 1) if s <= y <= e else 0.0
    e27 = A["ebuses_2025"] + A["ebuses_added_2026"] + A["ebuses_added_2027"]
    stock_prev, rows, eib, gb, lease_pay = A["ebuses_2025"], [], 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
    for y in FM_YEARS:
        cap = A["ebuses_2025"] + sum(v[0] for v in proj.values() if v[3] <= y)
        price = ((1 - A["artic_share"]) * A["price_12m"] + A["artic_share"] * A["price_18m"]) * (1 + A["escalation"]) ** (y - 2026) * A["price_factor"]
        plan = (A["ebuses_2025"] + A["ebuses_added_2026"] if y == 2026 else e27 if y == 2027 else
                min(ze_max, math.floor(e27 + (ze_max - e27) * (y - 2027) / (A["target_year"] - 2027) + 0.5)))
        renew = A["renew_2031_35"] / 5 if 2031 <= y <= 2035 else 0
        depot = sum(phased(v[1], v[2], v[3], y) for v in proj.values()) + phased(*cont, y)
        depot_own = depot * (1 - A["caas_share"])
        n_money = max(0.0, A["self_fin"] + depot_own * A["eu_grant_share"] + A["borrow_cap"] - depot_own) * 1000 / (price * max(1e-9, 1 - A["lease_share"]))
        limits = {"deliveries": A["delivery_cap"] - renew, "chargers": cap - stock_prev, "money": n_money - renew}
        add = plan - stock_prev if y <= 2027 else int(max(0, min(plan - stock_prev, *limits.values())))   # 2026-27 contracted
        stock = stock_prev + add
        bus_value = (add + renew) * price / 1000
        leased = bus_value * A["lease_share"] + depot * A["caas_share"]          # financed by a lessor or CaaS provider
        lease_pay += leased * annuity                                            # each year's new leases add a level payment
        capex = bus_value + depot                                                # programme value, owned or leased
        own_capex = capex - leased
        self_used = min(own_capex, A["self_fin"])
        grant_used = min(own_capex - self_used, depot_own * A["eu_grant_share"])
        need = max(0.0, own_capex - self_used - depot_own * A["eu_grant_share"])
        eib += need * A["eib_share"]; gb += need * (1 - A["eib_share"])
        binding = "" if (y <= 2027 or stock >= ze_max or add >= plan - stock_prev) else min(limits, key=limits.get)
        rows.append(dict(year=y, plan=plan, ebuses=stock, added=add, renewals=renew, bought=add + renew, self_fin_meur=self_used,
                         grants_meur=grant_used, eib_meur=need * A["eib_share"], bonds_meur=need * (1 - A["eib_share"]),
                         charging_capacity=cap, capex_meur=capex,
                         borrowing_meur=need, interest_meur=eib * A["eib_rate"] + gb * A["gb_coupon"], leased_meur=leased,
                         lease_payments_meur=lease_pay, binding=binding))
        stock_prev = stock
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    done = df.loc[df.ebuses >= ze_max, "year"]
    y100 = int(done.min()) if len(done) else 2041
    w = df[df.year <= 2035]
    b = df.binding[df.binding != ""]
    return dict(year_100=y100, ze_share_2030=round(100 * (int(df.loc[df.year == 2030, "ebuses"].iloc[0]) + A["h2_buses"]) / A["fleet_total"], 1),
                capex_2026_35=round(w.capex_meur.sum(), 1), peak_capex=round(w.capex_meur.max(), 1),
                max_borrowing_yr=round(w.borrowing_meur.max(), 1), interest_2035=round(w.interest_meur.iloc[-1], 1),
                cng_writeoff_meur=round(sum(n * u * max(0, r - y100) / 12 / 1000 for n, r, u in fm_cng(A)), 1),
                cng_retired_early=int(sum(n for n, r, _ in fm_cng(A) if r > y100)), peak_added=int(w.added.max()),
                peak_bought=int(round(w.bought.max())),
                peak_bought_year=int(w.loc[w.bought.idxmax(), "year"]),
                funding_2026_35={k: round(w[c].sum(), 1) for k, c in (("self-financing", "self_fin_meur"), ("EU grants", "grants_meur"),
                                                                       ("EIB", "eib_meur"), ("green bonds", "bonds_meur"))},
                leased_2026_35=round(w.leased_meur.sum(), 1), lease_payments_2035=round(w.lease_payments_meur.iloc[-1], 1),
                first_binding=b.iloc[0] if len(b) else "none"), df

fm_base, fm_base_df = fm_run()                 # rev. 13, the base of section 10 (D9)
fm_rev13 = fm_run(**FM_REV13)[0]
fm_aligned = fm_run(**FM_ALIGNED)[0]
display(pd.DataFrame({"rev. 13 (base)": fm_base, "File 4 conventions (comparison)": fm_aligned}))
w = fm_base_df[fm_base_df.year <= 2035]
print("What the 2033 plan asks for each year:")
display(w.assign(bought=w.added + w.renewals)[["year", "added", "renewals", "bought", "capex_meur", "borrowing_meur"]].round(1).set_index("year").T)
check("Port reproduces the financial model rev. 13: EUR 1,943.5 m and 100 % in 2033", abs(fm_rev13["capex_2026_35"] - 1943.5) < 0.1 and fm_rev13["year_100"] == 2033,
      f"EUR {fm_rev13['capex_2026_35']} m, {fm_rev13['year_100']}")
check("D9: section 10 runs on rev. 13 (the base equals the documented model)", fm_base == fm_rev13)
print(f"Comparison on File 4's conventions (2,210 buses, 13-year life, constant prices, no grants): EUR {fm_aligned['capex_2026_35']} m, "
      f"100 % in {fm_aligned['year_100']}")

10.1 · Tornado: which lever moves the 100 % year most¶

Each lever is moved alone, on a base with likely capacity (230 buses/yr, EUR 150 m/yr borrowing) and no delays, so one lever's effect is not hidden by others being unlimited. The depot levers are also run with buses and money unlimited, to show their effect in isolation.

In [27]:
REALISTIC_CAPACITY = dict(delivery_cap=230, borrow_cap=150)          # likely capacity, no delays
LEVERS = [  # name, optimistic, pessimistic (see LEVER_EVIDENCE)
    ("Borrowing per year", dict(borrow_cap=250), dict(borrow_cap=100)),
    ("Buses delivered per year", dict(delivery_cap=300), dict(delivery_cap=159)),
    ("Bus price", dict(price_factor=0.9), dict(escalation=0.04)),
    ("Entrevias grid and works", dict(delay_entrevias=0), dict(delay_entrevias=2)),
    ("Las Tablas ready", dict(delay_las_tablas=0), dict(delay_las_tablas=2)),
    ("Other depot retrofits (grid)", dict(delay_retrofit=0), dict(delay_retrofit=2)),
    ("La Elipa ready", dict(delay_la_elipa=0), dict(delay_la_elipa=1)),
    ("Charger cost per position", dict(charger_keur=57), dict(charger_keur=203)),
]
rows = []
for name, lo, hi in LEVERS:
    a, b = fm_run(**{**REALISTIC_CAPACITY, **lo})[0], fm_run(**{**REALISTIC_CAPACITY, **hi})[0]
    rows.append(dict(lever=name, year_optimistic=a["year_100"], year_pessimistic=b["year_100"],
                     year_swing=b["year_100"] - a["year_100"], capex_swing_meur=round(abs(b["capex_2026_35"] - a["capex_2026_35"]), 1),
                     binding_when_pessimistic=b["first_binding"]))
TORNADO = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(["year_swing", "capex_swing_meur"], ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
display(TORNADO)
print("Depot levers alone (buses and money unlimited):",
      {n: fm_run(**kw)[0]["year_100"] for n, kw in [("Las Tablas +2", dict(delay_las_tablas=2)), ("Las Tablas +3", dict(delay_las_tablas=3)),
                                                   ("Entrevias +2", dict(delay_entrevias=2)), ("all grid +2", dict(delay_entrevias=2, delay_retrofit=2, delay_las_tablas=2))]})
check("Tornado: every lever tested in both directions", len(TORNADO) == len(LEVERS))
for r in TORNADO[TORNADO.year_swing < 0].itertuples():
    print(f"Reversal: '{r.lever}' pessimistic finishes earlier ({r.year_pessimistic} vs {r.year_optimistic}). With money binding, a later "
          "depot spreads its capex over more years and frees cash for buses in the meantime: a cash-timing effect, not a benefit.")

10.2 · Most realistic case, and what 2033 would need¶

Every lever at its likely value: 230 buses/yr (EMT's 2019–20 pace), EUR 150 m/yr borrowing (the pitch's condition 4), and one-year slips at Las Tablas, Entrevías and the remaining depot retrofits. The grid shows how far more borrowing and faster deliveries pull the year back. These runs use rev. 13 (2,239 buses, 12-year renewals, 2 %/yr price growth, 20 % EU grants on depot works). Notebook 01 §8 frames the same question on File 4's conventions: 2037–2040 if purchases stay at 165–200 a year (gas buses then run past 13 years), and 2036 if every bus is renewed at 13 years as in File 4's S0, with purchases peaking near 380 a year.

10.2c · Payback and CO₂ of the 2033 and 2037 paths (report Annex C8)¶

Both paths are rev. 13 as ported above: the 2033 plan as built and likely capacity with no delays (230 buses and EUR 150 m of borrowing a year), with the aim-for-2030 run beside them. CO₂ uses File 4's own factor per bus switched from gas, read from File 4, with its mid-year convention, so it compares with S0 and S1. Savings use rev. 13's inputs: 101.9 M bus-km over 2,239 buses, gas at EUR 0.37/km, 1.30 kWh/km at EUR 0.15/kWh, and EUR 45/t on gas from 2028. Net present cost = capex − energy and carbon savings − value left in the buses at end 2040 (straight line over a 12-year life, the purchase year counted as a year of use), 2026-40. Plain constants, printed only: nothing here is written to Files 1-4.

In [30]:
# Report Annex C8: payback and CO2 of the 2033 and 2037 paths, and the discounted view (financial-model.md 4.4). Printed only.
C8_KM_BUS = 101_903_622 / FM["fleet_total"]          # rev. 13: EMT bus-km 2025 over 2,239 buses
C8_GAS_EUR_KM, C8_GAS_2023_EUR_KM = 0.37, 0.58        # rev. 13 gas cost per km; 2023 value as the high-price case
C8_KWH_KM, C8_ELEC_EUR_KWH = 1.30, 0.15               # brief consumption; rev. 13 electricity price
C8_CARBON_EUR_T, C8_CARBON_FROM = 45, 2028            # ETS2 price-stability trigger, on gas from 2028
C8_CHARGER_KEUR, C8_GAS_BUS_KEUR = FM["retrofit_keur"], 291   # one charging position; gas bus (2021-23 cohort price)
C8_RATES = (0.02, round((FM["eib_rate"] + FM["gb_coupon"]) / 2, 3), 0.05)   # base 3.3 % = mean of EIB rate and bond coupon

_f4 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(OUT, "File_4.csv")).sort_values(["scenario", "year"])
_cng0 = NB01["fleet"] - B25["n_bev"] - B25["n_h2"]
_sw = _f4.groupby("scenario").n_cng.transform(lambda s: _cng0 - s)
_mid = (_sw + _f4.groupby("scenario").n_cng.transform(lambda s: _cng0 - s.shift(fill_value=_cng0))) / 2
C8_T_BUS = float((_f4.co2_avoided_t / _mid).iloc[-1])                    # t CO2 a year per bus switched (File 4)
C8_F4_KM_BUS = 124_600_000 / NB01["fleet"]                               # File 4 basis: GTFS-scaled bus-km over 2,210 buses
C8_T_BUS_FM = C8_T_BUS * C8_KM_BUS / C8_F4_KM_BUS                        # the same bus on rev. 13's km (carbon price)

def c8_path(df, r):
    d = df.set_index("year")
    sw = (d.ebuses - FM["ebuses_2025"]).astype(float)
    mid = (sw.shift(fill_value=0) + sw) / 2
    co2_kt = C8_T_BUS * mid / 1000
    energy = mid * C8_KM_BUS * (C8_GAS_EUR_KM - C8_KWH_KM * C8_ELEC_EUR_KWH) / 1e6
    carbon = mid * C8_T_BUS_FM * C8_CARBON_EUR_T / 1e6 * (d.index >= C8_CARBON_FROM)
    disc = 1 / (1 + r) ** (d.index - 2026)
    price = ((1 - FM["artic_share"]) * FM["price_12m"] + FM["artic_share"] * FM["price_18m"]) * (1 + FM["escalation"]) ** (d.index - 2026)
    left = ((d.added + d.renewals) * price / 1000 * np.clip(1 - (2040 - d.index + 1) / FM_BUS_LIFE, 0, None)).sum()
    return dict(capex=d.capex_meur.sum(), capex_disc=(d.capex_meur * disc).sum(),
                npc=(d.capex_meur * disc).sum() - ((energy + carbon) * disc).sum() - left / (1 + r) ** (2040 - 2026),
                co2_2035=co2_kt.loc[:2035].sum(), co2_2037=co2_kt.loc[:2037].sum())

FM_BUS_LIFE = 12                                       # rev. 13 e-bus life (ebus_life_years)
C8_PATHS = {"aim for 2030": fm_run(target_year=2030)[1], "2033 plan": fm_base_df, "2037 (likely capacity)": likely_cap_df}
c8 = pd.DataFrame({k: {"net cost, undiscounted": c8_path(d, 0)["npc"], **{f"npc at {r:.1%}": c8_path(d, r)["npc"] for r in C8_RATES},
                       "capex 2026-40": c8_path(d, 0)["capex"], f"capex at {C8_RATES[1]:.1%}": c8_path(d, C8_RATES[1])["capex_disc"],
                       "CO2 kt 2026-35": c8_path(d, 0)["co2_2035"], "CO2 kt 2026-37": c8_path(d, 0)["co2_2037"]}
                   for k, d in C8_PATHS.items()}).round(1)
display(c8)
_gap = {r: c8_path(fm_base_df, r)["npc"] - c8_path(likely_cap_df, r)["npc"] for r in (0.0, *C8_RATES)}
_dco2 = c8_path(fm_base_df, 0)["co2_2037"] - c8_path(likely_cap_df, 0)["co2_2037"]
s0_co2_2035 = _f4[_f4.scenario == 0].co2_avoided_t.sum() / 1000
print(f"CO2 per bus switched from gas: {C8_T_BUS:.3f} t a year (File 4, mid-year); {C8_T_BUS_FM:.2f} t on rev. 13's {C8_KM_BUS:,.0f} km")
print(f"To 2037 the 2033 path avoids {_dco2:.1f} kt more than the 2037 path; S0 (File 4, 2,210 buses) avoids {s0_co2_2035:.1f} kt to 2035")
print("Net cost, 2033 path minus 2037 path (EUR m): " + ", ".join(f"{g:.1f} " + (f"at {r:.1%}" if r else "undiscounted") for r, g in _gap.items()))
print(f"Cost per extra tonne avoided to 2037: EUR {_gap[0.0] * 1e3 / _dco2:,.0f}/t undiscounted, EUR {_gap[C8_RATES[1]] * 1e3 / _dco2:,.0f}/t at {C8_RATES[1]:.1%} "
      f"(EUR {_gap[C8_RATES[1]] * 1e3 / (_dco2 * C8_KM_BUS / C8_F4_KM_BUS):,.0f}/t if CO2 is counted on rev. 13's bus-km)")

# Payback of one e-bus and its charging position against a gas replacement (2026 prices, undiscounted)
_ebus = (1 - FM["artic_share"]) * FM["price_12m"] + FM["artic_share"] * FM["price_18m"]
_extra = _ebus + C8_CHARGER_KEUR - C8_GAS_BUS_KEUR
_save = lambda gas: C8_KM_BUS * (gas - C8_KWH_KM * C8_ELEC_EUR_KWH) / 1000
_carbon = C8_T_BUS_FM * C8_CARBON_EUR_T / 1000
print(f"Payback: e-bus EUR {_ebus:.1f}k + position EUR {C8_CHARGER_KEUR}k - gas bus EUR {C8_GAS_BUS_KEUR}k = EUR {_extra:.1f}k extra; "
      f"saves EUR {_save(C8_GAS_EUR_KM):.1f}k energy + EUR {_carbon:.1f}k carbon a year -> {_extra / (_save(C8_GAS_EUR_KM) + _carbon):.0f} years "
      f"({_extra / (_save(C8_GAS_2023_EUR_KM) + _carbon):.0f} at the 2023 gas cost of EUR {C8_GAS_2023_EUR_KM}/km); "
      f"paying back in {FM_BUS_LIFE} years needs EUR {(_extra / FM_BUS_LIFE - _save(C8_GAS_EUR_KM) - _carbon) / C8_KM_BUS * 1000:.2f}/km more")
check("C8: File 4's CO2 per switched bus is the same every year (one factor, mid-year)",
      bool(((_f4.co2_avoided_t / _mid).round(2).nunique() == 1)), f"{C8_T_BUS:.3f} t")
check("C8: neither path pays back within the bus life", _extra / (_save(C8_GAS_EUR_KM) + _carbon) > FM_BUS_LIFE)

10.2d · The recommended 2035 path, depot by depot (report Annex C9)¶

The depot-by-depot roadmap in scenarios/roadmap_2035.py (rules and assumptions N1–N10 at the top of that file, explained in notes/roadmap-2035.md), run on File 4's 2,210 buses with EMT's budgeted 70 and 65 e-buses in 2026–27. Bus prices rise 2 % a year from 2026 as in rev. 13; depot and grid costs are not escalated, as in rev. 13. Funding follows rev. 13: EUR 35 m a year of EMT funds, EU grants for 20 % of depot and grid works, the rest borrowed, half from the EIB at 3.0 % and half in green bonds at 3.6 %, no repayments. The two depot sensitivities change one date each; the model has no borrowing limit, so a borrowing cap is not run here. Plain constants, printed only: nothing is written to Files 1–4.

In [31]:
# Report Annex C9: the recommended 2035 path from the depot-by-depot roadmap model (scenarios/roadmap_2035.py). Printed only.
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(BASE, "scenarios"))
import roadmap_2035 as RM

C9_SET = {**RM.A, "order_2026_27": {2026: 70, 2027: 65}}       # EMT 2026 budget and 2027 draft budget (notebook 01 section 8)
C9_RATE = FM["eib_share"] * FM["eib_rate"] + (1 - FM["eib_share"]) * FM["gb_coupon"]   # 3.3 % on the debt drawn so far

def c9_run(a=C9_SET, entrevias_grid=None):
    """Roadmap run; entrevias_grid moves only Entrevias' grid upgrade, and Las Tablas' connection follows a['las_tablas_open']."""
    conn0 = RM.connection
    def conn(d, y):
        if d == "Entrevias" and entrevias_grid: return 0.9 if y < entrevias_grid else 14.0
        if d == "Fuencarral": return 4.3 if y < a["las_tablas_open"] else a["las_tablas_mw"]
        return conn0(d, y)
    RM.connection = conn
    try:
        return RM.run(a)
    finally:
        RM.connection = conn0

c9_D, c9_Y, c9_M, c9_RL, c9_I, c9_K = c9_run()
_esc = (1 + FM["escalation"]) ** (c9_K.year - 2026)
_bus = (c9_K.eur * _esc)[c9_K.group == "buses"].groupby(c9_K.year).sum() / 1e6
_dep = c9_K[c9_K.group == "depot"].groupby("year").eur.sum() / 1e6
c9 = c9_Y.set_index("year")[["gas_replaced", "ebus_renewals"]].astype(int)
c9["buses_meur"], c9["depots_meur"] = _bus, _dep.reindex(c9.index, fill_value=0.0)
c9["investment_meur"] = c9.buses_meur + c9.depots_meur
c9["eu_grants_meur"] = FM["eu_grant_share"] * c9.depots_meur
c9["borrowing_meur"] = (c9.investment_meur - c9.investment_meur.clip(upper=FM["self_fin"]) - c9.eu_grants_meur).clip(lower=0)
c9["interest_meur"] = c9.borrowing_meur.cumsum() * C9_RATE
display(pd.concat([c9, c9.sum().to_frame("total").T]).round(1))

_switched = c9.gas_replaced.cumsum()
_mid = (_switched.shift(fill_value=0) + _switched) / 2
_co2_35 = C8_T_BUS * _mid.sum() / 1000
_co2_37 = _co2_35 + C8_T_BUS * 2 * _switched.iloc[-1] / 1000                       # 2036-37 with the whole gas fleet switched
_e2030 = int(c9_D[c9_D.year == 2030].ebuses.sum())

10.3 · Two models: rev. 13 and File 4's conventions¶

Rev. 13 is the base of this section (D9). Beside it, the same four cases run on File 4's conventions (FM_ALIGNED): 2,210 buses from the fleet register (D1; rev. 13 uses EMT's 2025 accounts, 2,239), e-bus renewals at a 13-year life (D2; 174 renewals in 2031–35 instead of 329), constant 2025 prices (rev. 13: +2 %/yr) and no EU grants (rev. 13: 20 % of depot works). Depot projects are unchanged; the balancing retrofit item and the oldest CNG cohort absorb the fleet difference. The tornado is shown on both.

10.4 · Leasing and charging-as-a-service: can they relieve the funding limit?¶

Money is the most at-risk lever (10.1). Two ways to buy without borrowing up front are already used in Spain:

  • Bus leasing: EMT Madrid itself tendered finance leases for 81 buses in 2012 (BOE) and 66 in 2011 (BOE), and its budget books show about EUR 43 m and EUR 72 m of new finance leases in 2023 and 2024 (notes/financial-model.md).
  • Operating leases plus charging-as-a-service: Zenobē and Vectalia (Alicante) signed a framework of up to EUR 120 m in June 2026, covering electric buses, depot electrification as charging-as-a-service, energy management and battery-health risk (electrive). Endesa offers charging-as-a-service for bus depots and serves 850+ e-buses in Spain (Endesa).

Outside Europe, Shenzhen (not a File 1 city) electrified its whole fleet with bus groups leasing e-buses over about 8 years from bank leasing arms (China Development Bank Leasing, CCB Financial Leasing), taking ownership at the end; charging and maintenance suppliers carried battery-pack costs, and charging sites were opened to taxis and private cars to raise their use (WRI, World Bank). Opening depot chargers by day is one way a charging-as-a-service contract could earn more than the overnight bus load.

In the model, a lease share of each year's bus purchases and a charging-as-a-service share of depot works leave the borrowing cap and turn into a level yearly payment over the lease term. Deliveries and chargers still limit the pace. The term is EMT's own: 12 years in both its 2011 and 2012 lease tenders (10 years allowed as a variant in 2011). No lease rate is published (the tenders allowed fixed or Euribor-linked), so the rate is an assumption above Spain's 10-year yield, 3.802 % at the 5 Nov 2026 auction, and swept.

Caveats: leasing changes when EMT pays, not how much; payments become operating costs, funded mainly by the regional subsidy (EUR 441.5 m in 2026). A finance lease usually still counts as public debt under ESA 2010; only arrangements where the lessor carries most of the risk can stay off it, which IGAE decides.

Research questions, checked 23 Nov 2026:
  - (1) CNG-to-battery kit for EMT's city buses: NONE. Approved kits are for coaches or diesel buses; the only CNG repower programme (US) closed. Every retrofit number is a what-if
  - (2) Grid path: the PNIEC's 2030 factor, on the national basis, is 37.1 gCO2/kWh, used as the 2035 sensitivity; no official 2035 value exists. The base case keeps the flat 108.4 (Red Electrica 2025, verified) so these runs stay comparable with File_4
  - (3) Deliveries after 2027: no EMT tender yet; the 2033 target implies about 270/yr; 12-15 months from order to delivery, so 2028 buses need a 2027 tender
  - (4) Fast charge for a conversion: plug only, at most 150 kW, no pantograph, no European example in service. The top-up lever stays at zero and is swept

Not modelled here:
  - Opex: electricity against CNG price per km. Decides the business case and is not in P
  - Deadheading km from depot to terminal: section 5 now publishes terminal-to-depot km, so this is a join away and is still not in the energy figures
  - Grid connection lead times and civils, which may bind harder than money
  - Battery replacement inside a retrofit's extended life
  - Residual value of the chargers, and of a retrofitted bus's body beyond the age cap
  - Driver and workshop retraining, and the cost of the rotation CNG buses' extra year
